test_title: PYST 32: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 22 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which Fundamental Right guarantees Freedom of Speech, Assembly and Movement?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Freedom**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Right to Freedom** is provided under **Articles 19 to 22** of the **Indian Constitution**. It ensures essential freedoms to all citizens.
 
• **Article 19** guarantees six fundamental freedoms, including **freedom of speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession.**
 
• These freedoms are subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by the state in the interests of **sovereignty, integrity, public order, morality, decency, and security of the state.**
 
• **Freedom of Speech:** This ensures the right to express thoughts and opinions freely, including through oral communication, written words, or any other medium.
 
• **Freedom of Assembly:** This allows people to gather peacefully without arms for protests or meetings, provided it does not disturb public order or security.
 
• **Freedom of Movement:** This ensures citizens can travel freely anywhere within the country, promoting unity and integration.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Right to Freedom.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• **Right to Equality:** Provided under **Articles 14-18**, this ensures equality before the law, prohibition of discrimination, and equality of opportunity in public employment.
 
• **Right to Cultural and Educational Rights:** Under **Articles 29-30**, this protects the rights of minorities to conserve their culture and establish educational institutions.
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies:** Under **Article 32**, this allows individuals to move to the Supreme Court to enforce their fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **Reasonable Restrictions:**
 
 
• The **freedoms under Article 19** are not absolute. The state can impose restrictions for reasons like national security, public order, or morality.
 
• **Examples:** Freedom of speech does not include incitement to violence or hate speech. Similarly, freedom of assembly must be peaceful and without arms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 19 Specifics:**

 
 
• Freedom of profession ensures that every citizen has the right to pursue any occupation, trade, or business.
 
• However, the state can regulate certain professions in the interest of public health, safety, or other factors.
 
 
 
• **Landmark Cases:**
 
 
• **Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978):** The Supreme Court expanded the scope of personal liberty under Article 21, linking it with Article 19.
 
• **Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015):** The Supreme Court struck down Section 66A of the IT Act, ensuring protection of free speech online.
